title: Failover load shedding behavior notes (Hosted + Dedicated) — retry-after + streaming expectations
content:
Context
- This is a working notes doc for how we want the data plane + gateway to behave when regional failover is in progress OR when we detect regional impairment but have not yet completed a routing flip.
- The point is to reduce cascading failure: when a region is degraded, client retries + gateway retries can amplify load, and we can end up with multi-region overload (or flip-flopping).
- These notes are meant to align serving-runtime, API gateway, and routing/policy engine expectations before the Q1 controlled failover game day.

Non-goals
- Not trying to redesign routing policy in this doc (ADR-042/043 cover hierarchy + rollback).
- Not trying to specify every SDK detail. We just need clear, consistent wire semantics (status codes, headers) that clients can safely implement.

Terminology (for these notes)
- “Failover in progress” = routing/policy has begun shifting traffic away from Region A to Region B (could be partial by route/model/tier).
- “Overload” = we are dropping/shed at some layer (gateway, queue admission, runtime admission) because we cannot safely accept more work.
- “Streaming” = server-sent events (SSE) / chunked responses for chat/completions.

Design principles
1) Prefer fast, explicit rejection over slow timeouts.
   - If we know we can’t serve, return quickly with a structured response that encourages backoff and avoids retry storms.
2) Make overload responses distinguishable from “bug” 5xx.
   - On-call + dashboards need to separate capacity overload vs actual software errors.
3) Retrying must be bounded.
   - Retry budgets: small number of retries, jittered, and never unbounded loops.
4) Streaming disconnects are expected during region flips.
   - The system should help clients reconnect cleanly (idempotency guidance + redirect handling), but we should not promise perfect continuity.

Current observed failure modes (from rehearsals + incidents)
- Gateway retries on upstream timeouts caused multiplicative request volume during impairment.
- Clients retry immediately on 5xx and/or reconnect streaming without jitter, spiking connection count.
- During partial routing flip, some clients see a redirect to another region but treat it as fatal; others retry to the old region.
- “Slow fail” during impairment: long tail latency makes dashboards look “kinda fine” while customer experience is bad; eventually queues build and we start timing out (worst outcome).

Proposed behavior: status codes + headers

A) Overload / load shedding response
- Use 429 (Too Many Requests) for “we are healthy but currently overloaded / protecting the system”.
  - Historically 429 is rate limiting, but it’s also the most widely-implemented client backoff path.
  - We should include a reason code to distinguish user quota vs regional overload.
- Use 503 (Service Unavailable) for “region is impaired / failover in progress / upstream unavailable”.
  - For 503, always include Retry-After.

Header + body conventions (proposal)
- Retry-After: <seconds> (integer).
  - Keep simple; seconds only.
  - Include jitter on server side so large client populations don’t synchronize.
- x-redwood-overload: true
- x-redwood-overload-reason: one of:
  - region_failover_in_progress
  - region_capacity_exhausted
  - admission_shed
  - upstream_timeout_budget_exceeded
- x-redwood-request-id: always
- Body (JSON): include a stable machine-readable error code + message.
  - Example:
    {
      "error": {
        "code": "overloaded",
        "type": "transient",
        "message": "Temporarily overloaded; retry after 2s",
        "retry_after_seconds": 2
      }
    }

Notes
- For Dedicated: we need to be careful that 429 doesn’t look like customer rate limiting; we should always include x-redwood-overload-reason.
- For Hosted: 429 could collide with real quota/rate limit; therefore require x-redwood-overload-reason and distinct body error codes:
  - rate_limited (quota/rate-limit)
  - overloaded (infrastructure/transient)

B) Redirect semantics (routing flip)
- If routing is flipping regions at the HTTP layer (or client-visible), use 307 Temporary Redirect (preserve method) when safe.
- If a request is not safe to redirect (e.g., streaming in progress, request body too large / already partially read), prefer an explicit transient failure (503 + Retry-After) rather than silent hang.
- Add x-redwood-redirected-from: <region> and x-redwood-region: <region> so we can measure how many times clients are bouncing.

C) Retry budgeting recommendations (what we should tell SDK/docs)
- For non-streaming requests:
  - Max 2 retries within a 10s window.
  - Exponential backoff with full jitter.
  - Respect Retry-After when provided.
  - Do not retry on 4xx except 429/408.
- For streaming:
  - If disconnect occurs before receiving any tokens/events, treat as a normal retryable request (subject to budget).
  - If disconnect occurs after partial output, behavior depends on idempotency support (see below). Default should be “do not auto-retry unless idempotency key is set”.

Streaming reconnection expectations

What we can reasonably promise
- During regional failover, active streaming connections may drop.
- Clients that reconnect may be routed to a different region.
- With an idempotency key (and if the route/model supports it), we can attempt best-effort replay/continuation, but we should not promise exact token-for-token continuation unless we explicitly implement resumable streaming.

What we should implement short-term (Q1/Q2)
1) Make reconnect safe via idempotency keys for streaming start.
   - If client provides Idempotency-Key (or x-redwood-idempotency-key), and disconnect happens before completion, reconnecting with same key should either:
     a) return the same completed response (if already done), or
     b) resume from buffered server-side output (if we store enough), or
     c) restart but with a clear response header indicating it restarted.
   - If we can’t do resume, at least do “dedupe” so we don’t execute the same expensive generation multiple times due to reconnect.
2) Ensure redirect handling doesn’t break SSE framing.
   - If we redirect, it must be before we start sending SSE bytes. After bytes are sent, redirect is not meaningful; we should close with a final event explaining transient failure.

Proposed SSE error event (if we have to terminate stream)
- Send an SSE event like:
  event: error
  data: {"code":"transient_disconnect","message":"Stream interrupted; retry with same idempotency key","retry_after_seconds":2}
- Then close the connection.

Gateway/runtime knobs during failover (implementation notes)

Admission control / shedding ordering
- Order of operations during impairment should be:
  1) Reduce retries/timeouts first (prevent work multiplication)
  2) Shed at admission before queues build (fast 429/503)
  3) Only then allow queues to grow (avoid “slow fail”)

Retry + timeout tuning proposals
- Gateway per-request timeout budget should shrink during detected impairment to avoid long tail holding resources.
- Disable automatic gateway retries on 5xx during declared regional impairment (or strictly cap to 0–1).
- Prefer returning 503 with Retry-After over waiting for upstream to time out.

Circuit breakers
- If upstream error rate / tail latency exceeds threshold, trip circuit breaker and immediately serve 503 + Retry-After.
- Critical: when circuit breaker trips, propagate x-redwood-overload-reason so we can correlate to failover signals.

Dedicated-specific considerations
- Dedicated pools can become overloaded when Hosted traffic spills into a region (shouldn’t happen by policy, but misroutes happen).
- During regional failover, Dedicated should keep stricter admission control:
  - “Protect dedicated baseline” mode: shed non-essential/low-tier requests first.
  - If we must shed Dedicated, shed quickly and clearly (avoid minutes-long timeouts for enterprise workloads).

Client-visible behavior matrix (draft)
- Healthy, capacity ok:
  - Normal 200/stream
- Healthy but overloaded (local):
  - 429 + Retry-After, x-redwood-overload=true, reason=admission_shed
- Regional impairment detected, failover not complete:
  - 503 + Retry-After, reason=region_failover_in_progress (or upstream_timeout_budget_exceeded)
- Post-failover (traffic shifted) but destination region near capacity:
  - 429/503 depending on whether it’s “protecting” vs “actually unavailable”. Prefer 429 if service is up but shedding.

Observability hooks we need (so we can validate in game days)
Metrics
- redwood_overload_responses_total{reason,route,tier,region}
- redwood_retry_after_seconds_bucket{reason,region}
- streaming_disconnects_total{phase=pre_first_token|mid_stream,region,redirected}
- idempotency_dedup_hits_total{route,region}

Logging
- When we return 429/503 due to overload, log a single structured event (sampled) with:
  - request_id
  - region
  - overload_reason
  - retry_after
  - route/model
  - tenant_tier

Dashboards / alerts
- Need an overlay showing policy flips + overload response rate (to see if we’re failing fast vs timing out).

Open questions / TODO
- Should we standardize on 429 for all shedding, including “failover in progress”, or reserve 503 for impairment? Current proposal is 503 for impairment to align with common semantics and status pages.
- Do we need a dedicated error code for “redirect required” (vs actually issuing 307)? There are cases where redirect is unsafe mid-stream.
- Idempotency key support surface: which endpoints/routes get it first? (Hosted chat streaming first, then completions, then Dedicated?).
- How much buffering (if any) do we want for streaming resume vs just dedupe?

Action items (owners tentative)
- Gateway: implement Retry-After + overload headers + reduced retries during failover signals (Peter / Vikram) [ENG-2419]
- Runtime: admission shedding reason codes; ensure fast-fail path doesn’t allocate large KV/cache (Vikram)
- Routing/policy: expose “failover_in_progress” as a signal the gateway can consume for tuning (Mina / Ravi)
- SDK/docs: document bounded retries + streaming reconnect guidance (Elliot Price + runtime input)
- Observability: build panels for overload reasons + streaming disconnect phases (Allison)

Appendix: recommended client guidance (draft copy)
- If you receive 429/503 with Retry-After, wait at least the indicated time before retrying. Add jitter.
- For streaming, always set an Idempotency-Key if you plan to auto-retry on disconnect.
- Limit automatic retries to 2; do not retry indefinitely.
- If you see repeated redirect/region changes, surface a warning in client logs and stop retrying (risk of loop).
